title: La Réunion fringing reef — thermal-stress bleaching (2016, 2019)
summary: La Réunion's west-coast fringing reefs (SW Indian Ocean, ~21°S) bleached in the 2016 Western Indian Ocean mass event (3rd global event, strongest in the region since 1998) and again in 2019, when about 41% of corals bleached at Saint-Leu. This POC drives a parametric bleaching trigger from NOAA Coral Reef Watch Degree Heating Weeks (DHW) over the reef sectors, calibrates it with a reef-resilience coefficient, and backtests the payouts against documented bleaching for 2009-2024. The real DHW caught both documented events (hit rate 1.0), but it also runs high in several years without a documented mass-bleaching (2009, 2017, 2021), so the trigger over-pays: that false-positive gap is the basis risk a Discovery audit exists to quantify. Note the 2024 4th global event, concentrated equatorward, largely spared these high-latitude reefs (DHW ~1).
